# Glossary: Biocomputer Software Engineering Terminology

## Terms A–M

**Action potential (spike)** – Brief (~1ms) electrical transient generated by a neuron's membrane depolarization; the fundamental unit of neural signaling.

**Closed-loop control** – Real-time feedback system continuously monitoring biological substrate state and adjusting stimulation parameters based on that state.

**Common-average referencing** – Signal processing technique subtracting the mean signal across all recording channels from each channel to cancel coherent common-mode noise.

**DMA (Direct Memory Access)** – Hardware mechanism allowing peripheral devices to transfer data directly to/from memory without CPU involvement, enabling efficient high-throughput data streaming.

**Excitotoxicity** – Neuronal damage or death caused by excessive excitatory stimulation/neurotransmitter exposure.

**Hardware abstraction layer (HAL)** – Software layer providing a consistent interface to hardware, hiding hardware-specific details from higher-level software.

**Local field potential (LFP)** – Slower (Hz–hundreds of Hz) electrical fluctuations reflecting summed synaptic activity of a neural population near a recording electrode.

**MEA (Multi-Electrode Array)** – Recording/stimulation substrate with many electrodes enabling simultaneous multi-site neural signal acquisition and stimulation.

**Multi-unit activity (MUA)** – Aggregate spiking signal from multiple neurons near an electrode, without attribution to individual source neurons.

---

## Terms N–Z

**NWB (Neurodata Without Borders)** – Community-standard data format for neurophysiology data, enabling interoperability and data sharing.

**Organoid intelligence (OI)** – Research direction exploring brain organoids as biological computing substrates.

**Population coding** – Neural information encoding distributed across the joint activity of many neurons simultaneously.

**PREEMPT_RT** – Linux kernel patch enabling real-time scheduling with reduced and bounded latency.

**RTOS (Real-Time Operating System)** – Operating system providing deterministic, bounded-latency task scheduling for time-critical applications.

**SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data)** – CPU instruction class operating on multiple data elements in parallel, enabling vectorized signal processing.

**Spike sorting** – Computational process attributing individual detected spikes to specific source neurons based on characteristic waveform shapes.

**STDP (Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity)** – Form of synaptic plasticity where synapse strength changes depend on the relative timing of pre- and post-synaptic action potentials.

**Watchdog timer** – Hardware timer that must be periodically reset by software; triggers a safety response (e.g., stimulation cutoff) if software fails to reset it within the allowed period.
